validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's operators/owners tab records Owner1="Venture Global LNG" at 100%, with no ref. Every independent source found (Kinder Morgan's own February 2020 Evangeline Pass Expansion Project fact sheet PDF, Natural Gas Intelligence, Coeus Energy) describes Venture Global LNG only as the customer/off-taker buying incremental firm transportation capacity for its Plaquemines LNG terminal -- never as an equity owner of the Evangeline Pass pipeline facilities. Kinder Morgan's own fact sheet is explicit and primary: 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. ("TGP"), a Kinder Morgan subsidiary, and Southern Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. ("SNG"), a Delaware limited liability company equally owned by subsidiaries of Kinder Morgan, Inc. and Southern Company, are proposing the Evangeline Pass Expansion Project.' It then lists the specific new/modified facilities: the two loop segments that sum to this row's 13.1-mile length are BOTH explicitly along existing TGP lines (Yscloskey Toca Lateral in St. Bernard Parish; the 500 Line in Plaquemines Parish), and Coeus Energy's June 3, 2025 article confirms Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. itself filed for and received FERC's final in-service authorization (May 29, 2025) for the last of these segments (the 4-mile Plaquemines Parish loop). SNG's own facilities under this same joint project (a new Rose Hill compressor station and new meter stations, all in Mississippi, funded in part via SNG leasing the new capacity to TGP) are physically separate from the linear pipe this row describes. So while SNG/Southern Company is a genuine joint participant in the broader two-company Evangeline Pass Expansion Project (relevant to the SegmentCost spec concern below, since EIA's cost split attributes $672M of docket-recorded cost to SNG's side of the joint financing/lease arrangement), the specific 13.1-mile, 36-inch PIPE this row's Length/Diameter/Location fields describe is TGP's own facility -- so Owner1 should read Kinder Morgan (100%, via TGP), not a 50/50 Kinder Morgan/Southern Company split and certainly not Venture Global LNG.

validity.researcher_notes: The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset originally tracked this project as a single undivided record (Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co, Evangeline Pass Expansion Project, $261.7M, docket CP20-50) in releases 2020-03 through 2024-01. Starting with the 2024-04 release, EIA re-split it into two sub-projects reflecting the two FERC dockets: 'Evangeline Pass Expansion Project (Phase 1)' -- Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co, $261.7M, docket CP20-50, in service 2024 -- and 'Evangeline Pass Expansion Project (Phase 2)' -- Southern Natural Gas Co., $672M, docket CP20-51, in service 2025. This row's own recorded SegmentCost ($672,000,000) and StartYear1 (2025) line up precisely with the SNG/CP20-51 record, which is why the prompt's own EIA comparison flagged SegmentCost and Status as 'differs' against the WRONG (superseded, undivided) pre-split EIA vintage -- against the correct post-split SNG record the sheet's cost, capacity, length, diameter and StartYear1 all match closely. HOWEVER, Kinder Morgan's own February 2020 fact sheet shows the physical facilities are NOT split the same way EIA splits the cost/docket: BOTH of the linear pipe loop segments that sum to this row's 13.1 miles are explicitly TGP facilities (Yscloskey Toca Lateral, St. Bernard Parish; 500 Line, Plaquemines Parish), while SNG's side of the project (per EIA's own Phase 2 project_notes) consists of a new Rose Hill compressor station and new meter stations in Mississippi, plus a like-for-like unit replacement at TGP's existing CS 527 -- none of which is the linear pipe. So the $672M SNG-docket cost this row currently carries almost certainly funds more than (and possibly does not even cleanly include) the 13.1-mile pipe itself; TGP's own $261.7M docket cost is arguably the better match for 'this segment's cost' specifically, given the row's Length/Diameter are TGP's facility. Flagging the mismatch rather than silently picking one -- this is a genuine attribution/scope ambiguity in how EIA's docket-based cost split maps onto GEM's segment-based schema, not a simple sourcing gap.
